cells.tense: You are seeing the shape of what is ending, and it reads cleanly from where you stand.
cells.act: choose the light to steer by and turn toward it
cells.ask: Name what this clearing is making room for, and turn toward it this week — no plan, no schedule, just that direction and your own plain wanting.
cells.core:
You can see what this clearing is for — why the thing is finishing, what it was holding up, what got opened when it started to go. That sight is what lets a person set something down without dragging it. You are not fighting the ending; you are seeing it accurately.

What the clearing points toward deserves one plain sentence from you, said in your own hearing and nowhere else. Something on the far side is already pulling at you. Turning toward it does not mean leaving yet — it means knowing which way you face, so the finishing happens behind you. The endings can keep going while you are already oriented.

cells.verb: reading the pattern underneath what is ending
cells.place: at the near edge of a clearing

cells.tense: You will have run every branch of this ending before you allow it to finish.
cells.act: give the mess a shape it can be carried in
cells.ask: Take one ending under way and give it a shape you can carry: a named stopping point, a clear boundary, a stated last time. Then the shape holds it, not you.
cells.core:
A clearing has not opened yet, and you are mapping it ahead of time. Every route the ending could take, every way it could go badly, every counter-move — walked already, and the walking has not stopped. Seeing how things work has become seeing how they might fail, and that has become a place to stand instead of a way through.

What breaks it is a shape. Give one ending near you a container — a date, a boundary, a stated stopping point — one that can be spoken in a sentence. Not the whole clearing; a single piece. The skill is real and it is yours. It just needs one object instead of all of them at once.

cells.tense: You were at the lip of a clearing whose ending had already happened.
cells.act: hand one thing on in the way you were handed it
cells.ask: Pass on something you were taught about endings — the timing, the leaving, the quiet after — exactly as it was given to you, to someone who is in one now.
cells.core:
You reached a clearing and stopped at the edge of it. What finished here finished already, but you have not been willing to call it finished, and you have kept your eyes on the surface — the practical facts, the logistics — without reading what any of it means. The pattern is there, and you have been declining to look up at it.

Depth comes back through other people before it comes back alone. Something someone taught you about endings is still in your hands. Pass it on plainly, the way it reached you, to a person who is standing where you were. Their asking will make you say what you know, and saying it is how the reading comes back to you.

cells.tense: You are steering this clearing with a hand you have not noticed.
cells.act: sit with someone in it without fixing it
cells.ask: Sit with someone in the middle of their own ending and don't fix it. Stay past the point where you would normally start offering solutions, and say nothing toward the answer.
cells.core:
In this clearing, patterns are running that you have not looked at. The endings are happening and you can see them, but not the pull in your own hand that keeps choosing them — so the shape of what is finishing seems like something that arrived, rather than something you are doing. Something in you is setting the terms here, and it has not been met.

Other people are where this gets found. When someone is in the middle of their own ending, stay with them and do not fix it. That is not advice and it is not rescue. What you notice while sitting there is the same thing that would let you see your own part in this clearing plainly, in your own voice.
cells.sheetLine: A pattern is shaping this ending. You have not claimed it.

The unsupported claim is any statement about what the person has actually ended, lost, or refused — the cells name the mechanism and the capacity's condition, not their history. The likely objection is that a reading about an abstract capacity can feel airless; the asks stay concrete so they survive being wrong. The sentence that would serve me more than the reader is any grand line about transformation itself — the cells avoid it and stay with the person's own pattern and their own endings.
